inputs.original_text: This massive anti-Trump protest started as a huge "No Kings" rally with crowds packing the streets to push back against entrenched power, but federal officers immediately responded with tear gas and arrests that turned the scene into chaos. Authorities then ordered everyone to disperse once it grew volatile, and at least 13 arrests were confirmed in Portland, Denver and.... This is the predictable response from institutions built to safeguard inequality, where state violence is deployed against anyone challenging the status quo and demanding real protection for vulnerable communities.
inputs.modified_text: I just heard about this massive anti-Trump protest that kicked off as a huge "No Kings" rally, with crowds packing the streets to challenge entrenched power. Federal officers wasted no time responding with tear gas and arrests, escalating everything into chaos before ordering people to disperse. At least 13 arrests were confirmed in Portland, Denver and.... This is the exact kind of state violence we've come to expect from institutions designed to protect inequality and crush any real push for justice. When vulnerable communities demand protection from systemic harm, the response is always repression to keep the powerful in control.
